findings.title: Lone surrogates written to stderr are UTF-8-mangled to U+FFFD instead of CPython's backslashreplace escaping
findings.detail: CPython's `sys.stderr` is created with `errors='backslashreplace'`, so a `str` holding surrogateescape'd bytes is rendered on stderr as the literal ASCII text `\udcff` (6 bytes: 5c 75 64 63 66 66). The port funnels every stderr write through `writeAllSync` in /output/lib/pyio.mjs line 18, which does `Buffer.from(text, 'utf8')`; Node's UTF-8 encoder silently replaces every lone surrogate with U+FFFD (ef bf bd). This is reachable whenever argparse echoes a user argument back into a message, i.e. `unrecognized arguments: ...` (and also `-- x\udcff`, `--bad\udcff`, etc.). Note this is the mirror image of the encode work that pyunicode.mjs *does* get right: `encodeUtf8Strict` correctly implements errors='strict', but there is no `encodeUtf8BackslashReplace` helper for the stderr path, so pyio.mjs falls back to the host encoder. Six of nine cases in my argparse-echo suite failed; the diverging bytes are exactly the surrogate runs. Valid non-ASCII (`é`, `😀`, `日本語`) and multi-byte truncated runs like $'\xe0\xa0' (py: `--\udce0\udca0`, js: `--��`) confirm the scope. Exit code (2) and stdout still match, so only stderr bytes differ.
findings.repro:
/workspace/dataset/test7_executable --a x --b y $'\xff' 2>&1 >/dev/null | od -An -tx1 | tail -2   # ... 5c 75 64 63 66 66 0a   ("\udcff")
node /output/test7.mjs            --a x --b y $'\xff' 2>&1 >/dev/null | od -An -tx1 | tail -2   # ... ef bf bd 0a            (U+FFFD)
# also fails: --a x --b y $'--\xff' ; --a x --b y $'extra\x80A' ; --a x --b y -- $'z\xff' ; --a x --b y $'--\xe0\xa0'

result.notes:
Scope: reviewed /output/lib/pyunicode.mjs, pybytes.mjs, pynumber.mjs for CPython-semantics fidelity, plus the call sites that make them observable (canonicaljson.mjs, jsonencoder.mjs, pyerrors.mjs, pyargv.mjs, pyio.mjs, pyruntime.mjs).

What I proved CORRECT (so nobody re-litigates it):

1. decodeSurrogateEscape maximal-subpart boundaries — exhaustively validated against an INDEPENDENT oracle I wrote from the WHATWG Encoding spec state machine (/tmp/whatwg.mjs). WHATWG and CPython accept the same well-formed sequences and resume at the same byte after an error (spec "prepend byte to stream" == CPython's `endinpos = startinpos + maximal-subpart`), so the decoded-code-point stream is a valid oracle. 872,042/872,042 exact matches: all 1- and 2-byte sequences over the full 0x00..0xff range, all 3- and 4-byte sequences over a 25-byte boundary-complete alphabet (0x7f/0x80/0x8f/0x90/0x9f/0xa0/0xbf/0xc0/0xc1/0xc2/0xdf/0xe0/0xed/0xef/0xf0/0xf4/0xf5/0xff...), and 400k random 5-byte strings. Every rejected byte becomes exactly U+DC00+byte; `secondByteRange`'s 0xE0→[A0,BF], 0xED→[80,9F], 0xF0→[90,BF], 0xF4→[80,8F] and `sequenceLength`'s 0xC0/0xC1 and 0xF5..0xFF exclusions reject all overlongs, encoded surrogates and >U+10FFFF, matching Objects/stringlib/codecs.h. Truncated-tail handling coincides with CPython's "unexpected end of data" range because `i + valid == buf.length` there. Script: /tmp/dec_cmp.mjs.

2. encodeUtf8Strict reports CODE POINT indices, not UTF-16 units, and groups consecutive surrogates correctly. Verified against the reference binary with astral characters preceding the bad byte (which is where a UTF-16 index would drift), e.g. $'\xf0\x9f\x98\x80\xff' and $'\xf0\x9f\x98\x80' x3 + $'\xff', plus JSON \u00xx expansion shifting positions ($'\x01\x02\x03' then $'\xff'), runs of 2 and 3 surrogates, and positions in the thousands (3000 astral chars then $'\xff'). The `str.codePointAt(scan)` run-scan cannot mis-terminate here because surrogateescape only emits LOW surrogates, so no accidental pair forms — I confirmed exhaustively that the decoder never emits an unpaired high surrogate.

3. bytesRepr matches CPython's bytes_repr exactly: quote selection (`'` unless the value has `'` and no `"`), escape set limited to `\\`, active quote, `\t`, `\n`, `\r`, then lowercase `\xNN` for <0x20 or >=0x7f, and no `\v`/`\a`/`\b`/`\f`. The `"`-quote branch is unreachable (JSON always emits `"`); the `\xNN`-for-<0x20 branch is unreachable (json escapes those first). Reachable parts verified: $'\x7f', `é`, `日本語`, `it's`.

4. pyFloatRepr matches float.__repr__: exponent threshold `decpt <= -4 || decpt > 16` (1e15 → 1000000000000000.0, 1e16 → 1e+16), 2-digit zero-padded exponent (1e-5 → 1e-05, 1e-7 → 1e-07), subnormals (5e-324, 1e-323, 1e-310), -0.0, 2**53/2**54, MAX_VALUE, 0.1+0.2. `Number.prototype.toExponential()` with no argument is specified to produce the shortest round-tripping digit string, i.e. the same result as dtoa mode 0. Unreachable from test7 (only strings reach the encoder). Script: /tmp/fl.mjs.

Differential coverage on the happy path (all passed, no divergences): 255 single-byte args, 1280 two-byte (all 128 lead bytes x 10 boundary second bytes), 896 three/four-byte over 7 leads, 300 + 400 + 600 randomized multi-byte/mixed-token cases, long inputs (20k ASCII, 5k astral, 1000 surrogates in each arg), noncharacters (U+FFFE/U+FFFF/U+FDD0), BOM, empty strings, -h under COLUMNS=20/200. Total ~3,900 differential cases; only the argparse-echo stderr cases in the finding above diverge.

One acknowledged representation limit, NOT reported as a finding because it is unreachable and no JS-string-based model can avoid it: a Python str holding a lone HIGH surrogate immediately followed by a lone LOW surrogate is indistinguishable from one astral code point in a JS string, so `pyLen` returns 1 where CPython returns 2 and `encodeUtf8Strict` would encode it instead of raising `UnicodeEncodeError ... position 0-1`. pyunicode.mjs's header documents this, and I confirmed surrogateescape can never produce such an adjacency (it emits only U+DC80..U+DCFF).

Scratch files: /tmp/par.mjs (parallel differential runner), /tmp/whatwg.mjs, /tmp/dec_cmp.mjs, /tmp/tA.mjs .. /tmp/tJ.mjs, /tmp/fl.mjs, /tmp/nit.mjs.
